title: Chocolate Ganache for Cupcakes: Ratios for Drips, Fillings and Whipped Frosting
summaryShort: The best ganache ratio for cupcakes depends on the job. Use 1:1 chocolate to cream by weight for drips and glazes, 2:1 for fillings and pipeable frosting, and 1:2 for whipped ganache.
metaTitle: Ganache Ratio for Cupcakes: Drips, Fillings, Whips
metaDescription: Get the right ganache ratio for cupcakes: drips, fillings, glazes and whipped frosting, plus fixes for split ganache. Use our chart and bake today.
sidebarBullets: Drip or glaze: 1:1 chocolate to cream by weight.
Filling or pipeable frosting: 2:1 chocolate to cream.
Whipped ganache: 1:2 chocolate to cream, chilled overnight.
Milk chocolate needs about 1.5 times more chocolate than dark.
White chocolate needs about 2 times more chocolate than dark.
Drip at 85 to 90°F for a clean edge.

sections.heading: The Basic Ganache Ratio for Cupcakes
paragraphs: Ganache is just chocolate and hot cream, and the ratio by weight decides what you can do with it. A 1:1 mix pours as a glaze, 2:1 sets firm enough to fill or pipe, and 1:2 whips like cream.
Always weigh both ingredients in ounces or grams. Cups of chopped chocolate are too inconsistent, and a small error changes the set a lot.
list: 1:1 (equal parts): soft glaze and drips.
2:1 (more chocolate): thick filling, truffle-style center, pipeable swirl.
1:2 (more cream): light, whippable frosting.

sections.heading: Ratios for Drips, Fillings and Glazes
paragraphs: For a drip on a cupcake, use 1:1 dark chocolate to cream, such as 4 ounces chocolate and 4 ounces cream. That covers about 12 cupcakes with a thin, shiny coat.
For a filling, use 2:1, such as 6 ounces chocolate and 3 ounces cream. It cools into a spoonable center that will not leak into the crumb.
list: Thin glaze for dipping: 1:1, used at 90°F.
Thicker drip that stays in place: 1.5:1, used at 85°F.
Filling: 2:1, cooled until it holds a soft peak on a spoon.

sections.heading: How Dark, Milk and White Chocolate Change the Ratio
paragraphs: Milk and white chocolate need more chocolate per ounce of cream because they have less cocoa solids and more sugar and milk. Dark chocolate sets firmest, so it can take the most cream.
Use the table above as your starting point. If your chocolate is labeled 70 percent cacao or higher, add a splash more cream, since high-cacao bars set very firm.
list: Dark (55 to 70 percent): 1:1 for drips, 2:1 for fillings.
Milk: 1.5:1 for glazes, 2:1 for drips, 2.5:1 for fillings.
White: 2:1 for glazes, 2.5:1 for drips, 3:1 for fillings.

sections.heading: Temperature for a Clean Drip
paragraphs: Drip ganache at 85 to 90°F for a clean, even edge. Warmer than that, it runs off the cupcake and puddles on the liner.
Cooler than 85°F and it turns thick and clumpy. Test by lifting a spoon: the ganache should fall in a slow, smooth ribbon.
list: Heat cream until steaming, about 180°F, not boiling.
Pour over finely chopped chocolate and wait 2 minutes.
Stir gently from the center outward.
Cool, stirring now and then, until it hits 85 to 90°F.
Chill the frosted cupcakes for 10 minutes to set the drip.

sections.heading: How to Make Whipped Ganache Frosting
paragraphs: Whipped ganache uses 1 part chocolate to 2 parts cream for a light whip, or 1:1 for a denser, fudgier one. For 12 cupcakes, try 4 ounces chocolate and 8 ounces cream.
Chill it at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, until it feels like cold pudding. Whip on medium speed for 1 to 3 minutes until it holds a soft peak.
list: Stop as soon as it holds a peak, since overwhipping turns it grainy.
Pipe right away with a large open star tip.
Keep cupcakes in the fridge until serving in warm rooms.

sections.heading: How to Fix Split or Grainy Ganache
paragraphs: A split ganache looks oily or curdled because the fat has separated from the water. Fix it by adding 1 to 2 tablespoons of warm milk or cream and stirring slowly, or by blending with an immersion blender.
Grainy ganache usually means the cream was too hot or the chocolate seized. Warm it gently over a pot of hot water, stir in a little cream, and it should smooth out.
list: Oily and split: add warm cream, 1 tablespoon at a time.
Grainy after whipping: melt gently, re-chill, and whip less.
Too thick: add warm cream, a teaspoon at a time.
Too thin: add chopped chocolate and stir until melted.

howToSteps: Weigh the chopped chocolate and cream using the ratio for your job.
Heat the cream until steaming, about 180°F, then pour it over the chocolate.
Wait 2 minutes, then stir gently from the center outward until glossy.
For a drip, cool to 85 to 90°F and spoon it over chilled cupcakes.
For a filling, cool until thick, then pipe or spoon into cored cupcakes.
For whipped ganache, use 1:2 chocolate to cream, chill overnight, and whip to soft peaks.
Fix split or grainy ganache with a little warm cream and slow stirring.

faq.question: What is the best ganache ratio for cupcake drips?
faq.answer: Use 1:1 dark chocolate to cream by weight. Cool it to 85 to 90°F before spooning it over the cupcakes.

faq.question: How much ganache do I need for 12 cupcakes?
faq.answer: A 4 ounce chocolate and 4 ounce cream batch covers 12 cupcakes with a drip. For whipped frosting, use 4 ounces chocolate and 8 ounces cream.

faq.question: Why is my white chocolate ganache so runny?
faq.answer: White chocolate has no cocoa solids, so it sets softer. Use at least 2:1 white chocolate to cream for drips, and 3:1 for fillings.

faq.question: Can I make whipped ganache without chilling overnight?
faq.answer: A 4 hour chill can work, but it must feel cold and thick all the way through. If it is still soft in the center, it will not hold a peak.

faq.question: How do I fix grainy ganache?
faq.answer: Warm it gently over hot water and stir in 1 to 2 tablespoons of warm cream. An immersion blender also helps bring it back to smooth.
